title: CC DataStore
description: A connection descriptor for a storage backend. Field names taken verbatim from json struct tags in USACE/cc-go-sdk datastore.go (DataStore).

name.description: How DataSources and plugin code reference this store. Must be unique within its scope; duplicate names resolve first-match-wins in cc-go-sdk GetStore, which is an open contract question.

store_type.x-cc-known-divergence: Only S3 (FSS3) and FS (FSB) are registered in DataStoreTypeRegistry by registerStoreTypes(). WS, RDBMS and EBS are declared constants with no registered implementation, so a payload naming them fails at connectStores with 'Unregistered store type'. TileDB is a separate unregistered package. The enum lists what the code can NAME; only S3 and FS currently WORK. An SDK MUST report an unregistered-but-valid type as 'unsupported backend', not as a schema violation.

profile.description: Prefix applied to environment variable lookups when connecting. profile 'MYSTORE' means credentials and endpoint are read from MYSTORE_AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, MYSTORE_AWS_REGION and so on. Absent or empty means no prefix.
profile.x-cc-note: FS stores do not open a connection and therefore do not need a profile. Field name is 'profile' on the store; the payload-scoped env var CC_PROFILE is a different thing (cc-go-sdk CcProfile = "CC").

params.description: Backend-specific parameters. Both S3 and FS honor 'root' as a prefix applied to every path in this store.

root.description: Root prefix/folder for resources in this store. cc-go-sdk GetAbsolutePath defaults it to "/" when absent via GetStringOrDefault("root", "/").

params.x-cc-note: Typed as PayloadAttributes in Go (map[string]any), so values are not guaranteed to be strings. Do not add additionalProperties: {type: string} here; the Go-generated schema does and it is wrong at runtime.
